bug_semantics: OliveTin's Logout RPC expired the browser's olivetin-sid-local cookie but did not revoke the corresponding SID in server-side SessionStorage. Authentication continued to resolve a replayed SID through GetUserSession until its roughly one-year expiry, so anyone retaining the old cookie remained authenticated after the user appeared to log out; the same design later also cleared the OAuth2 cookie without deleting its server-side state.
flaw_origin: Commit 8686a5629e6a8fae3d99f2af0a3e8c3c0c37aae0 turned the previously nonfunctional Logout stub into a user-visible logout flow by setting MaxAge=-1 on the client cookie, but it omitted any server-side deletion even though the request's authenticated user carried the provider and SID and authentication trusted the stored SID. This is the smallest commit that first wrote the advisory's clear-client-cookie-only mechanism; later cookie/security edits preserved it until the fix.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file -p 8686a5629e6a8fae3d99f2af0a3e8c3c0c37aae0` shows author and committer `jamesread <contact@jread.com>` and only the subject `fix: User Information panel and login/logout flow`; the BIC commit object has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories/GHSA-gq2m-77hf-vwgh identifies replay of an old SID after Logout, affected versions `< 0.0.0-20260304233115-d6a0abc3755d15`, patched pseudo-version `0.0.0-20260304233115-d6a0abc3755d15`, fix commit https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/commit/d6a0abc3755d43107be1939567c52953bcbec3d5, and fixed release https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/releases/tag/3000.11.1.

At BIC 8686a5629e6a8fae3d99f2af0a3e8c3c0c37aae0, service/internal/api/api.go:330-350 implements Logout and line 348 sends an expired cookie; service/internal/auth/sessions.go:62-80 still retrieves and returns `sessionStorage.Providers[provider].Sessions[sid]`, with no revocation call in Logout.

`git log main -L 545,570:service/internal/api/api.go` follows the current Logout function back through later edits and shows 8686a5629e6a8fae3d99f2af0a3e8c3c0c37aae0 as the commit that first replaced the stub with cookie-expiration behavior. `git log main -S'MaxAge:   -1' -- service/internal/api/api.go` likewise identifies 8686a5629e6a8fae3d99f2af0a3e8c3c0c37aae0 as the earliest local-cookie logout implementation; 7425db53f652b55d87449767176c8a3691b42601 only added the analogous OAuth2 cookie clear later.

Direct parent-tree verification: `git show 43cfe4137840cf52de95da8c2c15d217afc61148:service/internal/api/api.go` shows Logout only as a commented user lookup followed by `return nil, nil`; it contains no response, expiring cookie, Set-Cookie, or apparent-success logout flow. The 43cfe4137840cf52de95da8c2c15d217afc61148 parent nevertheless already registers one-year local SIDs in api.go:151/161 and accepts them via auth.GetUserSession in acl.go:222 and sessions.go:62, establishing that the BIC added client-only logout atop persistent SID authentication.

The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a merge or squash: its commit object names only parent 43cfe4137840cf52de95da8c2c15d217afc61148. `git log --graph --ancestry-path 43cfe4137840cf52de95da8c2c15d217afc61148..3000.1.2` shows the BIC as the concrete member commit below merge/release commits 2a21d74e and 1cb12b20, so those wrappers are not substituted for the smallest BIC.

Version boundary: `git tag --contains 8686a5629e6a8fae3d99f2af0a3e8c3c0c37aae0` includes 3000.1.2 (target 1cb12b203eadda98a3f1dd49d6ca6a6b85c36149, 2025-10-26) and later vulnerable releases, but omits 3000.1.0 and 3000.1.1. `git tag --contains d6a0abc3755d43107be1939567c52953bcbec3d5` starts at 3000.11.1 and omits 3000.11.0, matching the advisory's patched boundary.

Fix d6a0abc3755d43107be1939567c52953bcbec3d5 calls `auth.RevokeSessionForProvider(api.cfg, user.Provider, user.SID)` at service/internal/api/api.go:395 before clearing cookies. It adds RevokeSessionForProvider/RevokeUserSession in service/internal/auth/sessions.go:70-90, where line 87 deletes the SID from SessionStorage and persists the change, plus an OAuth2 revoker for its separate state store. This directly closes replay rather than merely changing the cookie.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p 8686a5629e6a8fae3d99f2af0a3e8c3c0c37aae0` reports human author/committer jamesread <contact@jread.com>, a plain one-line message, and no trailers or bot/AI marker. No later commit, PR metadata, branch name, or fix attribution was used for the verdict.
reasoning: The security boundary is server-side SID validity, not possession of the browser's current cookie jar. Before the BIC, local authentication already created a random SID, retained it for about one year, and authenticated any request presenting a SID found in SessionStorage, while Logout was only a nonfunctional stub. The BIC implemented the first apparent-success logout behavior: the UI called Logout and the API expired the browser cookie, but the commit never deleted the same SID from storage. Therefore a copied pre-logout cookie continued through GetUserSession and restored the user's identity. The exact vulnerable clear-cookie-only lines are absent from the immediate parent and first appear in the single-parent BIC; subsequent edits only expanded or hardened cookie clearing. The direct advisory fix finally passes the authenticated provider/SID to provider-specific revocation before cookie removal and is contained from release 3000.11.1 onward. Because the smallest BIC's own commit object is human-authored and contains no AI signal, the lifecycle is proven and the correct BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI.
